attributes.title: Preregistration: Block II Heredity, Reproduction and Population Change - Theory of Everything Research Programme.
attributes.description:
This preregistration freezes the first confirmatory study for Experimental Block II of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. Block II tests whether a collection of artificial agents constitutes a heritable reproducing population in which differential reproductive success generates cumulative population change, while separating reproduction, heredity, variation, causal reproductive differences and population-level selection effects.

Five matched population architectures are compared: reproduction without heredity (E0), heredity with random reproductive allocation (E1), heredity plus fitness-sensitive differential reproduction (E2), random search without lineage selection (E3), and within-lifetime optimisation without inheritance (E4). The study preregisters environmentally controlled parent-offspring transmission tests, paired inherited-trait interventions, selection-versus-control comparisons in two static ecological regimes, a fidelity-variation sweep and an environmental-switching experiment.

Twenty held-out independently initialised population seeds, individual and reproduction definitions, lineage criteria, mutation operator, genotype-phenotype mapping, direct-offspring reproductive-success measure, uncertainty procedures and Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules were frozen before confirmatory execution. Development-only pilots informed the thresholds and are excluded from confirmatory evidence. No held-out Block II population had been executed when the protocol was frozen, and the execution gate remains closed until this preregistration is public.

H2.5, robustness to alternative reproducing-unit definitions, is explicitly deferred because the current minimal ecology contains only one independently defensible reproducing unit. No second unit is manufactured post hoc.

A positive result would support only an artificial heritable reproducing population and selection-driven population change within the registered ecology. It would not establish the historical origin of biological reproduction, universal units of selection, inevitable evolutionary progress, intelligence, consciousness or biological life in every scientifically relevant sense. Related experimental programme: Craggs, K. (2026), Testing a Candidate Dependency Architecture: An Adversarial Experimental Programme for Maintenance, Heredity, Learning, Agency and Self-Modelling, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230.
tags: Theory of Everything Research Programme heredity reproduction natural selection population change artificial evolution causal intervention lineage analysis computational simulation evolutionary dynamics preregistration reproducibility open science artificial systems

344-2.value:
This study asks under what experimentally specified conditions artificial agents form a heritable reproducing population in which differential reproductive success generates cumulative population change.

The preregistered hypotheses are:

1. H2.1 - Heredity. Parent-offspring transmission creates reproducible hereditary dependence that survives environmental controls. Heredity must remain detectable after conditioning on the parent's local ecological optimum, and it must be selectively disrupted when the transmission channel is removed or parental labels are shuffled within the same environmental stratum.

2. H2.2 - Causal reproductive effect. Specified inherited variation causally alters expected reproductive success under the registered ecology. A paired do(g=0) / do(g=1) intervention must alter expected direct-offspring allocation under fitness-sensitive reproduction while leaving neutral reproductive allocation unaffected.

3. H2.3 - Selection-driven population change. Fitness-sensitive hereditary reproduction generates cumulative population change beyond matched neutral heredity, random search and within-lifetime optimisation. The effect must occur in both the selection ecology and a preregistered held-out inverted-preference ecology.

4. H2.4 - Fidelity-variation relation. Population adaptation depends systematically on the balance between transmission fidelity and generation of variation. With the favoured genotype initially absent, zero variation should prevent discovery, modest variation should permit hereditary amplification, and excessive transmission error should weaken retained adaptation.

5. H2.6 - Environmental switching. Environmental inversion produces a historically structured response in selected populations: prior adaptation is disrupted, selective direction reverses, and the population re-adapts. The matched neutral-heredity control should not reproduce the same systematic response.

H2.5 is deferred. The current ecology has only one independently defensible reproducing unit, the individual agent. A confirmatory alternative-unit test requires a later nested-unit ecology.

344-4.value: Data does not yet exist. No part of the data that will be used for this analysis plan exists, and no part will be generated until after this plan is registered.

344-14.value:
No confirmatory data for this preregistered study currently exists. None of the twenty registered confirmatory population seeds has been executed, inspected or analysed, and confirmatory execution is software-gated until the preregistration is public.

Development-only simulations were run before freezing the protocol. They validated individual identity, reproduction and lineage recording; demonstrated strong parent-offspring transmission under hereditary architectures and collapse of conditional parent-offspring information when transmission was removed or labels were shuffled within environmental strata; validated the paired inherited-trait intervention; established discriminating behaviour in two static ecological regimes; exposed a non-monotonic fidelity-variation relation; and validated environmental switching and re-adaptation. Those pilots are explicitly DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY, are excluded from confirmatory estimates and decision rules, and were used to choose pilot-informed thresholds.

The confirmatory seeds are disjoint from all Block II development seeds and from the earlier B1, B2 and H1.5 confirmatory seed sets. The six confirmatory manifests, referenced configurations, seed set, analysis RNG seeds and decision rules were frozen before registration. Any analysis introduced after confirmatory outcomes are observed will be labelled exploratory and will not replace a failed preregistered criterion.

value: Simulation study: Using existing or synthetic data to assess performance of a model, mimic operation of an existing or proposed system, or predict possible outcomes in a controlled context. This may include demonstration of methods, many varieties of modeling, prediction of policy impacts, simulating behavior or outcomes in a population, and other designs.

Direct inference on causal relationship(s): This study is intended to infer or estimate a causal relationship between two or more variables. It is designed specifically for the purposes of causal inference or identification.

344-38.value: No blinding is used because the study is entirely computational and the condition identity is part of the executable configuration. Researcher influence is instead constrained by a public preregistration, frozen manifests and SHA-256 locks, explicit held-out seeds, deterministic analysis RNG seeds, automated provenance validation and preregistered quantitative decision rules. Individuals are not manually classified and confirmatory populations are not selected for inclusion based on outcomes.

344-40.value:
This is a controlled computational population-simulation study. The primary confirmatory unit is an independently initialised population replicate. The same twenty registered seed identities are reused across matched conditions to permit paired population-level contrasts.

Five architecture classes are implemented: E0 reproduction without heredity; E1 heredity with random reproductive allocation; E2 heredity plus fitness-sensitive differential reproduction; E3 matched random search without lineage selection; and E4 within-lifetime phenotype optimisation without inheritance.

Six frozen manifests cover: H2.1 reproduction/heredity; H2.2 paired inherited-trait intervention; H2.3 in static Regime A; H2.3 in held-out static Regime B; H2.4 fidelity-variation sweep; and H2.6 environmental switching. Static population studies run for 40 generations. Fidelity-variation and switching studies run for 60 generations. Population size is 80.

The design deliberately separates reproduction, heredity, heritable variation, causal reproductive effects and cumulative population change. Natural-selection language is permitted only if the logically prior criteria survive their separate tests.

344-44.value: No experimental units are randomly assigned to treatment arms. Twenty explicit held-out seeds are preregistered. The same seed identities are used across matched conditions to support paired comparisons. Seeds are not selected, replaced or excluded according to scientific outcome.

344-47.value:
The study generates new computational population data. No human, animal or pre-existing observational dataset is sampled.

Each population begins with 80 artificial individuals with persistent identities. Reproduction creates distinct descendant identities and explicit parent-offspring lineage edges. The simulation records generation-level population metrics, individual states, direct offspring counts and lineage events. The static ecologies contain spatially heterogeneous resources and local genotype-optimum fields; H2.6 additionally inverts the optimum field at generation 25.

Confirmatory execution begins only after public preregistration and formal opening of the execution gate. All raw generation trajectories, lineage records, individual records, seed snapshots, manifest/configuration hashes and provenance metadata will be preserved.

344-51.value:
The confirmatory sample consists of twenty independently initialised population seeds. These are the primary replicate units.

Depending on the manifest, each seed is evaluated across multiple matched architecture or mutation-rate conditions. Individuals, generations and descendants within a population are nested observations and are not counted as independent confirmatory replicates.

The six confirmatory manifests comprise 60 population runs for H2.1; 40 paired population-level intervention assays for H2.2; 80 population runs in each of the two H2.3 ecological regimes; 140 mutation-rate population runs for H2.4; and 40 population runs for H2.6. Reuse of the same seed identities across matched conditions supports paired analysis and does not increase the independent population sample size beyond twenty per condition.

344-53.value: Twenty independent population replicates per condition were fixed prospectively after development validation and before confirmatory execution. The aim is reproducibility of large, preregistered hereditary and selection contrasts rather than estimation of a small biological population effect. The design combines magnitude thresholds, seed-consistency counts and population-level bootstrap uncertainty. No post-hoc sample-size increase is permitted because results are borderline or unfavourable.

344-55.value:
Development ends with the frozen version 1.0.0 confirmatory protocol. Confirmatory data collection begins only after this preregistration is public, all six manifest/lock pairs pass integrity verification, and the execution registry is changed to CLEARED_FOR_CONFIRMATORY_EXECUTION.

Data collection ends after every preregistered condition has completed valid execution for all twenty seeds. There is no early stopping based on scientific results. Technically invalid executions remain in the audit trail and may be rerun using the same seed after correction. No unfavourable valid population will be replaced by another seed.

344-58.value:
None, following the OSF instruction that non-randomised investigations should respond "none".

The simulation nevertheless contains prospectively specified deterministic condition differences and interventions: heredity present/absent; differential reproduction present/absent; random search; within-lifetime optimisation; genotype intervention; mutation/transmission-error rate; ecological regime; and environmental inversion. These are specified in the frozen design but are not randomised treatment assignments.

344-62.value:
The study records individual identity, parent identity, genotype, phenotype, position, local ecological optimum, performance, direct offspring count, population size, birth count, genotype frequencies, adaptive/favoured-variant frequency, binary genotype diversity, transmission fidelity, conditional parent-offspring information, trait-fitness covariance, Price-equation selection and transmission terms, environment phase, lineage depth/branching information and extinction status.

H2.2 additionally records expected direct-offspring allocation under paired do(g=0) and do(g=1) interventions. H2.4 records mutation rate and resulting transmission fidelity/adaptation. H2.6 records pre-switch, immediate post-switch and terminal adaptive-genotype frequencies plus time to regain the registered adaptation threshold.

Technical provenance variables include seed identity, manifest/configuration hashes, source/software version, raw-output hashes and provenance validation state.

344-66.value:
No composite evolutionary, organisation or constraint score is constructed.

Transmission fidelity is the proportion of parent-offspring events in which offspring genotype exactly matches parental genotype. Conditional hereditary information is I(Gp;Go|E), conditioning on the parent's local ecological optimum. Favoured-variant frequency is the proportion of living individuals carrying the genotype favoured by the registered static ecology. Adaptive-genotype frequency uses the currently favoured genotype after environmental switching.

The Price equation partitions change in the focal inherited trait into a differential-reproduction covariance term and a transmission/transformation term. These quantities are descriptive partitions and are not treated as causal proof by themselves.

Re-adaptation time is the first post-switch generation at which adaptive-genotype frequency reaches at least 0.75.

344-71.value:
Primary inference uses preregistered population-level estimands and decision thresholds rather than a single fitted omnibus model or primary p-value family.

H2.1 evaluates distinct reproduction, population-level transmission fidelity and conditional parent-offspring information, including a no-transmission architecture and within-environment-stratum shuffled-parent null. H2.2 evaluates the population-level mean of paired inherited-state intervention effects and a matched neutral-allocation control. H2.3 compares final favoured-variant frequency across E1-E4 in two static ecologies using paired seed-level differences; Price-equation terms are descriptive. H2.4 compares adaptation and observed fidelity across seven fixed mutation rates. H2.6 evaluates reversal and re-adaptation after environmental inversion in E2 relative to E1.

Continuous population-level uncertainty is estimated using percentile bootstrap intervals with 10,000 resamples and fixed analysis seed 20261008. H2.1 shuffled controls use 100 within-environment-stratum permutations with fixed seed 20261009. Individuals within one population are never treated as independent confirmatory replicates.

344-75.value: No outcome-dependent centering, standardisation, logarithmic transformation or recoding is planned. Genotype is binary and architecture, regime and mutation-rate conditions use fixed preregistered identifiers. Frequencies remain on their native [0,1] scale. Direct offspring allocation remains on its native expected-count scale.

344-77.value:
Inference follows the exact frozen Retain/Restrict/Reduce/Suspend/Reject rules in the attached preregistration record and manifests. H2.1-H2.6 receive separate decisions; H2.5 is DEFERRED before confirmatory execution.

Natural selection is retained as an effective mechanism in this artificial ecology only if reproduction/heredity, causal inherited-trait effects and cumulative selection-driven population change have each survived their separate registered tests. No multiple-testing correction is used because the hypotheses are not interchangeable searches for statistical significance and no pooled omnibus significance claim is made.

344-79.value:
All technically valid runs from every registered seed are included. No population or individual is excluded because its result is surprising, unfavourable or statistically extreme.

A run is invalid only for preregistered technical reasons, including manifest/configuration hash mismatch, unregistered seed, non-finite simulation state, corrupted required output or failed provenance/integrity validation. Scientific failure remains valid evidence. Extinction is an outcome and is not an exclusion criterion.

344-81.value: No statistical imputation is planned. Missing required output caused by technical execution failure results in an INVALID_RUN record and, where possible, rerun with the same preregistered seed after correction. If decisive evidence cannot be generated validly, the affected claim may receive SUSPEND. No new seed is substituted for missing or unfavourable scientific evidence.

344-83.value:
Secondary reporting includes population trajectories, lineage depth and branching, genotype diversity, extinction outcomes, trait-fitness covariance, Price-equation components and per-seed adaptation-time distributions. These analyses cannot replace failed primary thresholds.

Any new fitness definition, new reproducing unit, post-hoc mutation range, alternative adaptation threshold or additional ecological regime introduced after confirmatory outcomes are observed will be labelled exploratory or placed in a new preregistration.

344-86.value:
Block II follows the completed Block I programme but does not assume that Block I's artificial self-maintenance result is a universal prerequisite for reproduction. The ordering is methodological rather than a claim of necessary natural progression.

The present study is deliberately designed to prevent several common conflations: reproduction is not equated with growth; parent-offspring resemblance is not equated with heredity without a transmission channel; mutation and changing frequencies are not automatically called selection; within-lifetime optimisation is not treated as cross-generational selection; and Price-equation covariance is not treated as causal identification without the independent H2.2 intervention.

H2.5 is deferred because the current simulation does not contain a genuine second reproducing level. This is a prospective limitation, not a post-hoc exception.
